decisions.reason: The whisk selection impact is already fully captured by the candidate's message-64 MODIFY, including removal of the obsolete whisk-style reference; no additional change is required.
Selecting motor and control components that support 1500 RPM does not necessarily change the current requirement to provide a basic wiring plan with solenoid control wiring.
The selected whisk and 1500 RPM maximum do not change the established 2.5-quart bowl capacity or bowl geometry requirements.
The motor-speed and whisk-selection decision does not alter the spout material, appearance, or dispensing configuration.
A higher available maximum motor speed does not modify the existing splash-control target or conditional splash-guard policy.
The component-selection details do not change the requirement to deliver the initial system layout in CAD.
The whisk selection and motor-speed ceiling do not alter the solenoid-controlled dispensing sequence or its flow requirements.
The necessary 1500 RPM maximum is already fully represented by the candidate's message-64 MODIFY.
The source changes motor and whisk component constraints, not the DJ-style visual theme or decorative controls.
The 1500 RPM capacity does not itself change the requirement that the unit remain stable and avoid rattling or shifting during operation.
Selecting a particular whisk and motor-speed capacity does not change the existing strategy to use simple off-the-shelf prototype electronics.
The source decision does not change the requirement that bowls be quickly removable and swappable during events.
